$comment: Run learnings (crew src/learnings): when a run ends with evidence worth learning from (the operator's rulings, standing steers, the orchestrator's decisions, a reviewer's findings, a check that was red on the base or ran out of time), crew launches this one-seat, one-turn run on a seat that did NOT build the run (the builder never grades itself). It reads the handoff crew wrote (the evidence, what is already proposed) and writes report.json (its learnings and, per evidence item, kept or dropped and why); crew files each learning in the approve queue as a memory proposal attributed to the SOURCE run. Nothing is used until a person approves it. Cheap by design: no repository, nothing built, no floor, no judge (required_instruments is [] on purpose: a person judges each proposal). The run is never a person's to answer: if it stops at a gate (a short reply under the substance floor, a seat that crashed), crew stops it and files from report.json, or files the evidence raw when there is none.
title: Distill learnings
summary: Turns what a finished run went through into a few durable learnings, proposed for your review.
use_when: A run just ended and its record holds rulings, steers, decisions or review findings worth keeping

phases.instructions: You distil learnings; you never file them. Read the handoff file named in the task. It names the source run, its repository, `evidence` (each item: id, kind, text) and `already_proposed` (learnings already in the review queue), and report_path (the ONE file you may write). Keep only what passes the durability test: would this help a fresh session, on a different task, three months from now? Each kept learning states the rule, why it holds, and when it applies, in 1 to 3 plain sentences, and names its repository when it is about one. Good learnings: a test or check that fails under host load and why; a sandbox or seat limitation and its workaround; a repository rule or convention that bit; a pattern a reviewer flagged that would recur; a decision with its reason when it constrains future work; a standing preference the operator stated. Drop: progress or status (what was done, merged, shipped), anything only true of this one change, run ids, PR or issue numbers, commit SHAs, dates, and anything already in already_proposed. Never invent: every learning must be supported by an evidence item, and you name those ids. Write report_path as one JSON object: {"learnings": [{"kind": "gotcha|decision|pattern|steering", "content": "<1 to 3 sentences>", "evidence": ["<evidence ids>"]}], "checked": [{"evidence": "<id>", "kept": true|false, "why": "<one sentence>"}]}: at most 5 learnings, best first, and one checked entry for EVERY evidence item. An empty learnings list is a valid and common answer; the checked list is what makes it reviewable. Do not open, edit or run anything else: no repository, no tool that writes, no proposals (crew files those). Write report_path before you finish. Your reply is the review record, so write it out in full: first a line saying how many learnings you kept from how many evidence items ("Kept 0 of 1 evidence items: none found." when none), then one line per evidence item, "<id>: kept|dropped: <why, in one sentence>", then report_path's absolute path on the last line.
